headline: Lowest pay up 142%, Govt employees to get new pay scale arrears
summary: The Ministry of Finance has issued a gazette notification implementing the National Pay Scale 2026 retrospectively from July 1.
details: The Ministry of Finance issued a circular on September 17 implementing the National Pay Scale 2026, effective retrospectively from July 1. Government employees will receive arrears for the period between July 1 and the date the official order was issued.
This marks the largest pay hike for the civil service since independence, with the lowest pay increasing by a record 142 percent and the basic salary of top officials doubling.

The basic salary adjustments will be implemented in phases. For employees in Grades 10 to 20, 50 percent of the increase will be added from July 1 to December 31, 2026, rising to 75 percent from January 1 to June 30, 2027, and reaching 100 percent by July 1, 2027.
For officials in Grades 1 to 9, 40 percent of the increase will be disbursed from July 1 to December 31, 2026, rising to 70 percent from January 1, 2027, and reaching full adjustment by July 1, 2027.
All other allowances will continue at existing rates until December 31, 2027, with revised allowance rates taking effect on January 1, 2028.
The previous national pay scale introduced in 2015 saw basic pay rise by 95 percent in the top grade and 101 percent in the lowest.
caption:
Lowest pay up 142%! Govt employees will now receive arrears under the new National Pay Scale 2026.

The Ministry of Finance issued a circular on September 17 implementing the National Pay Scale 2026, effective retrospectively from July 1. Government employees will receive arrears for the period between July 1 and the date the official order was issued.

This marks the largest pay hike for the civil service since independence, with the lowest pay increasing by a record 142 percent and the basic salary of top officials doubling.

The basic salary adjustments will be implemented in phases. For employees in Grades 10 to 20, 50 percent of the increase will be added from July 1 to December 31, 2026, rising to 75 percent from January 1 to June 30, 2027, and reaching 100 percent by July 1, 2027.

For officials in Grades 1 to 9, 40 percent of the increase will be disbursed from July 1 to December 31, 2026, rising to 70 percent from January 1, 2027, and reaching full adjustment by July 1, 2027.

All other allowances will continue at existing rates until December 31, 2027, with revised allowance rates taking effect on January 1, 2028.

The previous national pay scale introduced in 2015 saw basic pay rise by 95 percent in the top grade and 101 percent in the lowest.

headline: 13-year-old missing boy found dead in Comilla jungle
summary: Ishayat Shahriyar, the son of a Comilla University teacher, was found dead in the Lalmai hills jungle after being missing for 22 hours.
details: The body of 13-year-old Ishayat Shahriyar, also known as Apratim, was recovered from the jungle of the Sananda area in Lalmai Hills, near Comilla University, on Saturday morning.
A local resident, Mohammad Abdul Kader Jilani, discovered the body while cutting bamboo. He noticed the child lying in the jungle with blood on his head.

Apratim was a seventh-grade student at Border Guard Public School in the Kotbari area. He went missing on Friday afternoon after leaving home with his mother's iPhone, telling his family he was going to take photos with friends.
Police recovered the body from the jungle around 1:00 PM on Saturday. Local sources and police reported that the child had signs of head injuries.
The mother's iPhone, which Apratim was carrying, is still missing. Police and university teachers suspect the boy was killed for the phone.

The body has been sent to Comilla Medical College Hospital for an autopsy. Comilla Sadar South Police Station OC Mohammad Rakibul Islam stated that police are working to identify the suspects involved in the loro murder.
